messages.author: cc776e2b2b1e08bf
messages.subject: Priors on stan_glmer
parts:
Hi everyone,

Thank you for developing the rstanarm package. It is very helpful.

I set up a model like below. Below I have 3 years of monthly data and I want to estimate year and month effects. Below, Year and Month are factors. Basically my prior for the Year coefficients are N(5, 1) and Month are N(0, 0.1).

stan_glm(y ~ 0+ Year + Month, prior=normal(c(rep(5,3), rep(0, 11)), scale=c(rep(1,3), rep(0.1, 11)), prior_ops=prior_options(scaled=F)) 

I wanted to set up a similar model using a hierarchical structure. When doing this, how do I set the same priors on the Year and Month coefficients? It doesn't seem to work the same way.

stan_glmer(y ~ 0 + (1|Year)+ (1|Month), prior= ???)

Thank you for the help.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Priors on stan_glmer
parts:
On Friday, January 27, 2017 at 5:41:46 PM UTC-5, Andy Medina wrote:
I wanted to set up a similar model using a hierarchical structure. When doing this, how do I set the same priors on the Year and Month coefficients? It doesn't seem to work the same way.

stan_glmer(y ~ 0 + (1|Year)+ (1|Month), prior= ???)

If you write the formula this way with (1|Year) and (1|Month), then the prior on the Year shifts is normal and the prior on the Month effects is normal, both with mean zero. This cannot be changed, but you can put a gamma prior on the standard deviations. See help(decov).

Ben

messages.author: cc776e2b2b1e08bf
messages.subject: Re: Priors on stan_glmer
parts:
Thank you Ben. That's good to know that the mean is zero, I can work with that. 

Am I able to set different priors for the different effects? Like for year effect, say I want it at Gamma (shape=1, scale=1) (Mean of 1) but Month ~ Gamma (shape =1, scale=0.1) (Mean of 0.1).

The below seems like it would be the right way to express this. Is this right? If not, how would I express it?

stan_glmer(y ~ 0 + (1|Year)+ (1|Month), prior_covariance=decov(regularization=1, concentration = 1, shape=1, scale=c(1, 0.1)), prior_ops=prior_options(scaled=F))

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Priors on stan_glmer
parts:
On Friday, January 27, 2017 at 6:56:04 PM UTC-5, Andy Medina wrote:
Thank you Ben. That's good to know that the mean is zero, I can work with that. 

Am I able to set different priors for the different effects? Like for year effect, say I want it at Gamma (shape=1, scale=1) (Mean of 1) but Month ~ Gamma (shape =1, scale=0.1) (Mean of 0.1).

The below seems like it would be the right way to express this. Is this right? If not, how would I express it?

stan_glmer(y ~ 0 + (1|Year)+ (1|Month), prior_covariance=decov(regularization=1, concentration = 1, shape=1, scale=c(1, 0.1)), prior_ops=prior_options(scaled=F))

I think that is right, except you are using an outdated version of rstanarm. Upgrade to 2.14.1 and then then the prior_ops argument is deprecated. Whether a prior is scaled or not is determined by the auto_scale argument to prior functions like normal(), student_t(), etc. In this case, there are no common predictors and so there are no priors on coefficients to scale.

Ben
